limitations: The supplied ME1-2017.pdf has zero readable pages. Its Power Plant chapter questions are represented through the solved book; full original-paper completeness cannot be certified from that damaged file.
Mains model solutions are independently derived self-assessment references, not official UPSC marking schemes.
Ten contradictory or disputed source items have explanations and are excluded from automatic scoring.

The bank covers the supplied Power Plant chapter and related nozzle, compressor, nuclear and renewable-energy questions. It is not a claim that every thermodynamics question is a Power Plant question.

notes: GATE ME 2020 repeated reaction question consolidated.
ESE auxiliary-consumption repeats consolidated; changed distractor sets retain their original source keys without invented option translations.
Linked questions with common data and different requested quantities remain separately answerable.

issues.title: GATE XE 2008 · Q29
issues.issue: Exit pressure0.1MPa contradicts the1.5bar property table supplied with the question.
issues.referenceAnswer: h2=2756.7+(50²−600²)/2000=2577.95 kJ/kg. Using the supplied1.5 bar table givesx≈0.948(optionD), but the stem says exit0.1 MPa, whose correct saturation data give a different quality.

issues.title: ESE Prelims 2006 · Book Q1.56
issues.issue: Printed answer table marks this question with an asterisk.
issues.referenceAnswer: Fan blade selection depends on duty, pressure, dust loading and manufacturer design; the supplied alternatives do not provide a reliable unique universal combination.

issues.title: ESE Prelims 2021 · Paper Q15
issues.issue: The supplied question has no uniquely supported listed answer.
issues.referenceAnswer: Pulverized firing gives high efficiency, rapid response to load changes and large steam capacity: statements 1, 2 and 4. Statement 3 is false; no offered combination is 1, 2 and 4.

issues.title: ESE Prelims 2019 · Paper Q44
issues.issue: The printed optimum velocity does not agree with the stated 6% relative-velocity loss.
issues.referenceAnswer: U/C1=cos18°/2=0.47553. With k=0.94, 120000=(1+k)C1²cos²18°/4 gives C1≈523.0 m/s. No option has that velocity; D gives the correct speed ratio but assumes no blade loss.

issues.title: ESE Prelims 2023 · Paper Q31
issues.issue: The supplied question has no uniquely supported listed answer.
issues.referenceAnswer: The speed ratio gives nozzle exit speed 144/0.48=300 m/s, so its actual enthalpy drop from rest is 300²/2000=45 kJ/kg. An isentropic heat drop additionally requires nozzle efficiency, which is not supplied. Blade velocity coefficient cannot substitute for nozzle efficiency.

issues.title: GATE XE 2008 · Q16
issues.issue: The supplied thermodynamic data give h≈1994.2kJ/kg with x≈0.766, but no option gives both values consistently.
issues.referenceAnswer: Isentropic exhaustx=(6.5422−0.4763)/(8.3960−0.4763)=0.76593; h≈1994.42 kJ/kgusing the supplied data; the closest combined choice isD (0.77, 2004.12).

issues.title: ESE Prelims 2023 · Paper Q34
issues.issue: The supplied question has no uniquely supported listed answer.
issues.referenceAnswer: The listed 99.31% is vacuum efficiency: 720/[765−(0.0533/1.013)×760]×100≈99.31%. Cooling-water condenser effectiveness is (25−15)/(34−15)=52.63%. A separate “under cooling efficiency” is not defined by the stem.

issues.title: ESE Prelims 2007 · Book Q1.61
issues.issue: The printed key gives increased air recirculation, which normally worsens cooling-tower inlet conditions. A reliable unique choice has not been established.
issues.referenceAnswer: Cooling capability improves as entering-air wet-bulb temperature falls. Recirculation brings warm humid exhaust air back to the inlet and usually degrades performance. The comparative mechanical-versus-natural-draft wording requires operating conditions not given here.

issues.title: GATE XE 2008 · Q26
issues.issue: The formula choices contain a printed exponent error; a reliable unique automatic choice is not assigned.
issues.referenceAnswer: Ideal Brayton maximum-work pressure ratio is (Tmax/Tmin)^[γ/(2(γ−1))]. The supplied scan instead prints γ/(2γ−1) in optionB, so no printed option exactly matches.

issues.title: ESE Prelims 2025 · Paper Q58
issues.issue: The generally correct combination is not among the supplied alternatives.
issues.referenceAnswer: Carnot requires reversible processes, so statement 2 is false. Statement 1 explains a practical limitation. A perfect gas with constant specific heat is not a necessary Carnot-cycle condition, so statement 3 is not generally true. The only generally correct statement is 1, absent from the options.
